questions.q: An API is best described as:
choices: A way for one piece of software to request data or action from another
questions.explanation: API stands for Application Programming Interface — a defined contract that lets one piece of software ask another to do something (like your weather app asking a weather service for tomorrow's forecast) without either one knowing the other's internals.

choices: Broadly, as a common data format across many languages and systems
questions.explanation: JSON was invented alongside JavaScript, but it's now the dominant data-exchange format everywhere: Python, Ruby, Go, Java, and every other modern language can read and write it natively. That universality is why it became the glue of the web.

questions.q: A browser blocks your fetch() call with a CORS error. What does that actually mean?
choices: The API server hasn't explicitly allowed requests from your origin
The browser is broken and needs a restart
You used the wrong HTTP method
questions.explanation: CORS blocks cross-origin requests unless the server explicitly permits them via an Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. The browser is working correctly — the fix is almost always on the API side, or routing the request through your own backend.
